gloss: offering (to gods, Buddha, or the deceased)

definitions.gloss: offering (to gods, Buddha, or the deceased)
definitions.explanation: Food, drink, or other items placed before a shrine, altar, or grave as a religious or spiritual offering.

examples.japanese: {仏壇|ぶつだん}にお{供|そな}えを{置|お}いた。
examples.english: I placed an offering on the Buddhist altar.

examples.japanese: お{正月|しょうがつ}にはお{供|そな}え{餅|もち}を{飾|かざ}ります。
examples.english: We display kagami mochi as an offering at New Year.

examples.japanese: お{供|そな}えの{果物|くだもの}を{下|さ}げて{家族|かぞく}で{食|た}べた。
examples.english: We took down the fruit offering and the family ate it together.

examples.japanese: {祖父|そふ}の{命日|めいにち}にお{供|そな}えとして{好|す}きだった{和菓子|わがし}を{選|えら}んだ。
examples.english: I chose Japanese sweets that my grandfather liked as an offering on his memorial day.

notes:
Refers to items offered to deities, Buddhist figures, or ancestors. The word uses the honorific prefix お and the noun form of {供|そな}える (to offer). After being offered, items are often "taken down" ({下|さ}げる) and consumed by the family, which is considered respectful sharing of divine blessings.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- お{供|そな}えを{上|あ}げる: make an offering
- お{供|そな}えを{下|さ}げる: take down an offering (to eat it)
- お{供|そな}え{餅|もち}: offering rice cakes (kagami mochi)
- お{供|そな}え{物|もの}: offering items (formal)
- {仏壇|ぶつだん}のお{供|そな}え: altar offerings

CULTURAL NOTE:
Common offerings include rice, fruit, sweets, sake, and water. At New Year, stacked round mochi called {鏡餅|かがみもち} are placed as offerings. The act of eating offerings after they have been presented is called お{下|さ}がり, and is seen as receiving blessings from the deity or ancestor.
